# NNPA Accelerator Path (selected sections)

The NNPA (Neural Network Processing Assist) is IBM's hardware accelerator for neural network inference, integrated into the z16 Telum processor. onnx-mlir routes supported ONNX ops to NNPA via a two-stage lowering: ONNX → ZHigh dialect → ZLow dialect → NNPA hardware calls.

## Build-Time Gate

NNPA-specific flags only exist in `--help` at all if onnx-mlir was built with the accelerator compiled in — a separate CMake option, not a compile flag:

```
-DONNX_MLIR_ACCELERATORS=NNPA
```

set at `cmake` configure time (`docs/AccelNNPAHowToUseAndTest.md`). Without it, every flag in this section is silently absent rather than erroring — check the build configuration before assuming a flag "doesn't work."

## NNPA Placement and Tuning Flags

Beyond accelerator selection and hardware level, `src/Accelerators/NNPA/Compiler/NNPACompilerOptions.cpp` defines the device-placement heuristic and a family of narrower optimization toggles.[^8] The heuristic (`--nnpa-placement-heuristic`) controls which qualifying ops actually get placed on NNPA absent a JSON override (see below):

| Value | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `QualifyingOps` (default) | Place every op that qualifies for NNPA |
| `FasterOps` | Place only ops that are actually faster on NNPA |
| `FasterOpsWSU` | `FasterOps`, accounting for stick/unstick conversion cost |
| `MuchFasterOpsWSU` | Same, with a larger required speedup margin |

Applied in `src/Accelerators/NNPA/Conversion/ONNXToZHigh/DevicePlacement.cpp`. The remaining `--nnpa-disable-*`/`--nnpa-enable-*`/`--nnpa-cpu-*` toggles in `NNPACompilerOptions.cpp`, grounded against their actual consumers (not just their own `desc()` text) — none of these have a `cl::location()`/`Opt`-suffix indirection; the `cl::opt` declaration itself is the variable every consumer below reads directly. This is a different convention from `CompilerOptions.cpp`'s (see [compiler.md](../../../../.agents/skills/onnx-mlir-internals/references/compiler.md)) — don't assume one implies the other when grounding a new flag in either file:[^11]

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|--------------|
| `--disable-zhigh-to-onnx` | false | Disables the post-optimization rewrite that converts a leftover `stick → elementwise op → unstick` chain back to a plain ONNX op (`createZHighToONNXPass` in `configurePassesNNPA()`) — skipped automatically when the placement heuristic is `FasterOpsWSU`/`MuchFasterOpsWSU`, since those already account for stick/unstick cost. Combined default: `--nnpa-placement-heuristic` defaults to `QualifyingOps` (neither of the two skip values), so **active out of the box** — the rewrite-back pass runs by default and is disabled only if this flag is explicitly passed (or made moot by switching to `FasterOpsWSU`/`MuchFasterOpsWSU`). No real command-line example found in docs/tests/wiki |
| `--disable-zhigh-decompose-stick-unstick` | false | Disables decomposing `zhigh.Stick`/`Unstick` into separate layout-transform + data-conversion steps (`ZHighDecomposeStickUnstickPass`/`ZHighRecomposeToStickUnstickPass`), which otherwise run so canonicalization/CSE can optimize the layout-transform half independently before re-fusing. Not gated by another flag. Example: `onnx-mlir --march=z16 --maccel=NNPA --disable-zhigh-decompose-stick-unstick --disable-compiler-stick-unstick --nnpa-disable-saturation --EmitMLIR --printIR %s` (`test/mlir/accelerators/nnpa/driver/data-transformation-on-ztensor.mlir`) |
| `--disable-compiler-stick-unstick` | false | Disables compiler-generated (as opposed to zdnn-library) stick/unstick code in `ZHighToZLow` lowering (`ZLowStickOptimizationPass`'s `expansion` argument). **Silently forced back to enabled (re-set to `false`) whenever `--nnpa-disable-saturation` is not also passed, on hardware level M14/z16 *or when `--march`/`--mcpu` is left unset entirely*** (the level-check treats "no march given" the same as z16) — z16 lacks hardware saturation support, so the compiler overrides the user's choice in `configurePassesNNPA()` rather than erroring. **Combined effect: this flag only takes effect if the user also passes `--nnpa-disable-saturation`, or targets `--march=z17`/`arch15` (M15).** Example: `onnx-mlir --march=z17 --maccel=NNPA --disable-compiler-stick-unstick --disable-fused-op --nnpa-disable-saturation --EmitMLIR --printIR -tag="test" %s` (`test/mlir/accelerators/nnpa/driver/ccfd.mlir`) — always paired with `--march=z17`/`arch15`-equivalent in real usage so the M14 force-override doesn't mask it, e.g. `utils/NNPAOpPerfModel/driver-zdnn-csu.sh` |
| `--nnpa-disable-saturation` | false | Controls whether DLF16 conversion during stick/unstick saturates out-of-range values (`getDefaultSaturation()` in `ZHighOps/OpHelper.cpp`), threaded through `ZHighToZLow.cpp`/`ProcessStickData*.cpp`); also the gate for `--disable-compiler-stick-unstick` above. Not itself gated. Example: `test/mlir/accelerators/nnpa/driver/saturation.mlir` (dedicated 3-RUN-line test toggling it across `--EmitZHighIR`/`--EmitZLowIR`) |
| `--nnpa-enable-scalar-bcast-binary` | false | Currently affects only `ONNXDivOp`: allows lowering a binary op with a scalar-broadcast operand to NNPA instead of forcing a CPU fallback (`isEnableScalarBcastBinary()` in `ONNXToZHighCommon.cpp`). Not gated by another feature flag (only by the universal NNPA hardware-level floor every op's legality is checked against). Example: `onnx-mlir-opt --march=z16 --maccel=NNPA --shape-inference --convert-onnx-to-zhigh --nnpa-enable-scalar-bcast-binary %s -split-input-file` |
| `--nnpa-cpu-dql` | false | Routes `DynamicQuantizeLinear`'s int8 quantization computation itself to CPU rather than NNPA, checked in `ONNXToZHigh.cpp`'s quantized-matmul lowering. **Not gated by `--nnpa-quant-dynamic`** despite the naming similarity — this pattern matches ONNX graphs that already contain an `onnx.DynamicQuantizeLinear` op (e.g. an externally pre-quantized model) and is inserted unconditionally, outside the `isDynQuant` block; its activation is IR-pattern-driven (does the graph already have this op?), not flag-driven. No real command-line example found in docs/tests/wiki |
| `--nnpa-cpu-dql-scale` | false | Narrower variant of the above: computes only the scale/zero-point (not the full quantization) on CPU — gates a canonicalization pattern (`QuantizedStickUnstickRemovalPattern`) in `ZHighQuantizedStickOp::getCanonicalizationPatterns`. Same non-gating finding as `--nnpa-cpu-dql` above — checked specifically and confirmed independent of `--nnpa-quant-dynamic`. No real command-line example found |
| `--nnpa-disable-shape-restriction` | false | Skips NNPA's static legality checks for dynamic-shaped inputs (`ONNXLegalityCheck.cpp`), assuming at compile time that dynamic dims will satisfy NNPA's constraints at runtime — a way to force-offload an op the static checker would otherwise reject, at the cost of a runtime failure if the assumption is wrong. See Static vs. Dynamic Shapes: What the Restriction Actually Checks below — "static" here is a compile-time-only distinction, not a hardware one. Not gated. Example: `onnx-mlir-opt --march=z16 --maccel=NNPA --shape-inference --nnpa-disable-shape-restriction --convert-onnx-to-zhigh %s -split-input-file` |
| `--nnpa-disable-fusion-op-stick-unstick` | false | Disables the `FusionOpStickUnstick` pass described above (collapses `unstick → op → stick` chains). Not gated. Example: `onnx-mlir --march=z16 --maccel=NNPA --printIR --EmitZHighIR --profile-ir=ZHigh -nnpa-disable-fusion-op-stick-unstick %s` |
| `--nnpa-disable-hugepage-malloc` | false | Disables replacing `malloc` with `OMHugePageMalloc` (`ReplaceMallocByHugePageMallocPass`), added when `emissionTarget >= EmitLLVMIR`. Gated by `emissionTarget` — satisfied by the default `--EmitLib`, so **active out of the box** (the pass runs, and this flag turns it off); only becomes moot if compilation stops before LLVM lowering. No real command-line example found in docs/tests/wiki |
| `--nnpa-disable-expand-attention-mask` | false | Skips the `ExpandAttentionMaskPass` that `addONNXToZHighPasses()` otherwise schedules once before the `RewriteONNXForZHigh` loop (see [ONNX-Level Rewrites Before ZHigh Lowering](#onnx-level-rewrites-before-zhigh-lowering)). Not gated by another flag; **active out of the box** (the pass runs, and this flag turns it off). Category `OnnxMlirOptions`, so it is an `onnx-mlir` driver flag; in `onnx-mlir-opt` the pass is invoked directly as `--expand-attention-mask`. No real command-line example found in docs/tests |

## ONNX-Level Rewrites Before ZHigh Lowering

`addONNXToZHighPasses()` (`NNPACompilerUtils.cpp`) first runs NNPA-motivated rewrites that stay in the ONNX dialect, so that more of the graph matches what zDNN accepts. Only then does it call `--convert-onnx-to-zhigh`.

**`--expand-attention-mask` (`ExpandAttentionMaskPass`).** This is a `func::FuncOp` pass defined in `src/Dialect/ONNX/Transforms/ExpandAttentionMask.cpp` / `Passes.td` and registered in `onnx-mlir-opt`. It is scheduled only by the NNPA driver: once, before the 3-iteration `RewriteONNXForZHigh` → `SimplifyShapeRelatedOps` loop, because it builds a `DimAnalysis` (expensive) on every run. It is on by default, and `--nnpa-disable-expand-attention-mask` skips it. It looks for `MatMul → [Mul] → Add → Softmax` chains: an `onnx.Add` whose result feeds an `onnx.Softmax`, whose two operands do not have the same shape per `DimAnalysis::sameShape()` (i.e. the mask broadcasts), and whose first operand is either an `onnx.MatMul` or an `onnx.Mul` with a MatMul on either side. When the Mul's other operand is a scalar tensor (the attention scale), that scale is recorded as well; a Mul by a non-scalar is looked through and only the mask is considered. Chains are grouped by mask (the Add's second operand) and, separately, by scale. A mask or scale is expanded when it is used by at least `minUses` = **4** chains and all of those chains' MatMul results have the same shape. In that case the pass inserts one `onnx.Expand` to that shape right after the first chain's MatMul, building the shape from constants for static dims and `onnx.Dim` for dynamic ones, and rewires every Add (mask) or Mul (scale, operand 1) to it. The result is that the Adds and Muls no longer broadcast, which matters because NNPA does not support every broadcast pattern (see [concepts/nnpa-broadcasting.md](nnpa-broadcasting.md)). Examples: `onnx-mlir-opt --expand-attention-mask %s -split-input-file` (`test/mlir/onnx/onnx_expand_attention_mask.mlir`, and `onnx_expand_attention_mask_with_mul.mlir` for the scale case).[^19]

**`RewriteONNXForZHigh` additions.** These are three new patterns, each paired with a dynamic-legality rule in `getRewriteONNXForZHighDynamicallyLegal()` that marks the matched op illegal so the conversion must rewrite it:[^20]

- **`onnx.Attention` → basic ONNX ops** (`AttentionForZHighPattern`). Every `onnx.Attention` not pinned to CPU by device placement is decomposed in place. The pattern only calls `lowerONNXAttentionOp()` from `src/Dialect/ONNX/Transforms/AttentionToONNXOps.cpp`, the same decomposition the CPU `ONNXToKrnl` lowering uses (the NNPA side keeps tensors, the CPU side runs it inside an `OpConversionPattern`). It picks one of two forms:
  - *Growing KV cache* (the default): 3D Q/K/V are split into heads (Reshape to `(B,S,N,H)`, then `Transpose [0,2,1,3]`) using `q_num_heads`; `past_key`/`past_value` are concatenated on axis 2; `Transpose(K)`; `MatMul(Q, Kᵀ)`; `Mul` by the scale; `Add` of `attn_mask` if given (an `i1` mask is first turned into a 0/−1e9 bias with `Where`, −1e4 for f16); `Add` of a constant causal mask if `is_causal` is set; `Softmax(axis=-1)`; `MatMul(·, V)`; and a merge back to 3D. `present_key`/`present_value` return the concatenated K/V when a past was given.
  - *Fixed-size KV cache*, used when `attn_mask`, `past_key` and `past_value` are all absent and `nonpad_kv_seqlen` is given: K/V are the whole padded cache, and the additive mask is built in the graph from `nonpad_kv_seqlen` (`Less`/`Where`) plus, with `is_causal`, a per-batch causal offset. Both K's and Q's sequence lengths must be static.
  - The `--kv-cache` compiler option overrides the choice: `Fixed` errors out unless the op has the fixed-cache operand pattern, and `Grow` forces the growing form.

  The scale is the `scale` attribute, or 1/√head_size when it is absent; the `Mul` is skipped when the scale is 1.0. `qk_matmul_output` is always none. The op is rejected with an error for GQA/MQA (`kv_num_heads` ≠ `q_num_heads`, or different head counts on 4D Q and K), non-zero `softcap`, `qk_matmul_output_mode` ≠ 0, a set `softmax_precision`, an `attn_mask` whose last dim is neither 1 nor K's sequence length, and an integer `attn_mask` other than `i1`. The pattern also fails if a 3D input's hidden dim is dynamic, or if `scale` is absent and the head size is dynamic. Since the legality rule makes every non-CPU `onnx.Attention` illegal, any of these failures fails the conversion. The resulting MatMul/Softmax/Add can each offload to NNPA on their own merits. Paired with `--enable-attention-op-construct` (see [stack/compiler.md](../../../../.agents/skills/onnx-mlir-internals/references/compiler.md)), this lets a recomposed attention subgraph come back out as NNPA-friendly ops.
- **`Reshape(3D→4D) → [Mul] → Add → Reshape(4D→3D)` → 3D `[Mul] → Add`** (`Rewrite4DAddTo3DPattern`, anchored on the final Reshape, benefit 1001). It fires when the `Add` does not broadcast (`sameShape`), its result is used only by that Reshape and `onnx.Dim` ops, at least one operand is a 3D→4D Reshape, and the operand ranks are (3,3), (3,4) or (4,3). An Add operand may also come from a `Mul` that does not broadcast and is used only by that Add and `onnx.Dim` ops. A 3D→4D Reshape feeding that Mul then counts as the Add's Reshape operand, and the Mul is rebuilt on 3D values. In the (3,3) case both 3D inputs must also have the same shape as the final 3D result. A 4D operand is collapsed to 3D with `reshapeTo3D`. Example: `test/mlir/accelerators/nnpa/conversion/rewrite-onnx-for-zhigh.mlir` ("Test basic 4D Add to 3D transformation", including a fully dynamic BERT-shaped case).
- **Split a non-last-two-dims transpose feeding MatMul B** (`rewriteMatMulNDto3D_NonBroadcast_SplitTransposeB`, z17/`arch15` only, `RewriteONNXForZHigh.td`). When B of a rank>3 `MatMul` is a `Transpose` whose permutation moves the last dim to second-to-last, e.g. `[0,2,3,1]` for Kᵀ in self-attention, the permutation is split into one that keeps the last dim in place (`[0,2,1,3]`) followed by a last-two-dims swap. The swap is absorbed by the transposed 3D MatMul that M15 supports. The rewrite is skipped if a static N or M exceeds the NNPA 3D-matmul dim limit, since `SplitLargeMatMulPattern` would then split the matmul and break the transpose. In the same commit, the existing transpose-A/B 3D patterns compute their result shape from the transpose *inputs* (`GetMatMulResultShapeTransA`/`TransB`/`TransATransB`), so the original transposes can become dead. Example: `test/mlir/accelerators/nnpa/conversion/rewrite-onnx-for-zhigh-arch15.mlir`.

## Op Fusion Before Lowering

A rewrite pass, `FusionOpStickUnstick` (`src/Accelerators/NNPA/Transform/ZHigh/FusionOpStickUnstick.cpp`, registered in `NNPAAccelerator::registerPasses()`, disabled with `--nnpa-disable-fusion-op-stick-unstick`), runs on the ZHigh dialect and collapses `unstick → op → stick`-adjacent chains so the op consumes/produces the ZTensor stick layout directly instead of round-tripping through unstick/stick. It recognizes five chain shapes, defined in `ZHighFusionOpHelper.hpp`/`.cpp` on top of the generic `FusionOpKindHelper` base (`src/Dialect/ONNX/Transforms/FusionOpHelper.hpp`). `docs/optimization-onnx-lowering/FusionOpPatterns.md` is the upstream catalogue of every kind (chain, match conditions, target idiom, lowering) — these five plus the CPU-side `simd-split-op-gather` kind, six in all — and is the primary source for this list:[^17]

- `zhigh.extended_layout_transform` — `LayoutTransform → [Reshape] → [Transpose] → [Reshape] → [LayoutTransform | DLF16ToF32 → [Mul by const scalar]]`, the attention head split/merge reshuffle between two NNPA ops. The innermost dim must be static and either a multiple of 64 or exactly 32 ("half sticks", `getExtendedLayoutTransformInnerTile()` in `ZHighOps/OpHelper.cpp`); with 32, every source half stick starts at offset 0 of its stick while the destination may start mid-stick (e.g. 12 heads of 32 merged into 384). The optional scalar `Mul` exists only after the F32 (`DLF16ToF32`) ending and must not broadcast. With `--disable-fused-op`, the same chain is instead rewritten into the composite `zhigh.ExtendedLayoutTransform` op, whose verifier accepts the same 64-multiple-or-32 innermost dims.
- `zhigh.expand-mul-stick` — `Unsqueeze → Expand → [Mul by const scalar] → Reshape → ZHighStickOp`, the GQA/MQA "repeat KV heads" idiom.
- `zhigh.concat-expand-stick` — `Concat(2 inputs) → Unsqueeze →` one of two tails: the 2-step `F32ToDLF16 → Expand → Reshape → LayoutTransform`, or the 1-step `Expand → [Mul by const scalar] → Reshape → ZHighStickOp`. It is the GQA/MQA "repeat KV heads after cache-concat" idiom (each concat input's innermost dim must be static mod 64). The scalar `Mul` is accepted only in the stick tail: in the 2-step tail the data is already DLF16 at that point, which the F32/I32/I64-only scalar extraction can never match. Lowers to one outer loop over the pre-concat dims plus two back-to-back tiled inner loop nests (one per concat input) that read-convert-and-fan-out directly to all `N` stickified output locations, instead of separate loops for the concat, the expand, and the stick (`ZHighToZLowFusedConcatExpandStickLowering`). If the concat result also has uses outside the chain (e.g. it's also threaded onward as the next layer's KV cache), the fused op grows a second result for it, filled by ordinary copy loops that share the same operand read as the fused path.
- `zhigh.unstick-split-heads` — `ZHighUnstickOp (3D/3DS) → Reshape (A,S,C)→(A,S,N,H,D) → [Transpose keeping D last] → Split (N outputs of size 1)`, the "split a fused QKV projection into heads" idiom. Requires static `N`, `H`, `D` with `D == 32` or `D % 64 == 0`, and `(H·D) % 64 == 0`. The fused op has `N` results, each in one of two modes: `f32` (the Split result itself; the following `Squeeze` stays outside and lowers to a zero-copy `memref.reinterpret_cast`), or `stick-3DS`, chosen when the Split result feeds only `Squeeze → Reshape (A·H,S,D) → ZHighStickOp (3DS)`. That chain is pulled into the body, and its sticks are copied as DLF16 with no dlf16→f32→dlf16 round trip.
- `zhigh.mul-add-stick` — `Mul(A0,A1)` and `Mul(B0,B1)` joined by `Add` or `Sub`, then `[Mul by const scalar] → Reshape (rank 3) → ZHighStickOp (3D/3DS)`. This is the rotary-embedding-before-attention idiom `(x·cos ± rotate_half(x)·sin)·k`. All four Mul operands must be non-constant F32 tensors that broadcast to the result only through static size-1 dims; the innermost dim must be 32 or a multiple of 64. One pattern is registered per join op (`FusedPatternsForMulAddStick` on `ONNXAddOp`, `FusedPatternsForMulSubStick` on `ONNXSubOp`). The producers of the Mul operands stay outside, so in the RoPE case it composes with the general `simd-split-op-gather` kind that produces `rotate_half(x)`. The lowering stores the computed expression straight into the stick, and none of the four F32 intermediates is allocated.

**Precedence between kinds.** Each `FusedPatternForOpKind<AnchorOpType, FusionT>` takes its `PatternBenefit` from the kind's `static constexpr int kMaxOpCount` (the longest chain the kind can match, which every `FusionOpKindHelper` subclass must define). Benefit only ranks patterns that share an anchor op type. `zhigh.concat-expand-stick` (anchored on `Concat`) can subsume a whole `zhigh.expand-mul-stick` chain (anchored on `Unsqueeze`), so `FusionOpStickUnstick::runOnOperation()` runs `FusedPatternsForConcatExpandStick` alone, to its own fixpoint, in a separate `applyPatternsGreedily` call *before* the main pattern set. Without that, the bottom-up worklist would let the shorter kind fire first and permanently consume the ops.[^17]

This pass is also where the **general, non-accelerator-specific** fusion kinds get formed on an NNPA build: it calls `populateONNXFusionOpPatterns()` (`src/Dialect/ONNX/Transforms/FusionOpTransform.hpp`) alongside its own `zhigh.*` kinds, so exactly one fusion pass ever runs. The CPU-side `--fusion-op-transform` pass that would otherwise form them is skipped whenever an accelerator is targeted — see [stack/dialect-onnx.md](../../../../.agents/skills/onnx-mlir-internals/references/dialect-onnx.md#--fusion-op-transform--the-cpu-side-formation-pass). `--disable-fused-op` turns both off.

A matched chain is replaced with a single `mlir::ONNXFusedOp` carrying a `kind` attribute (e.g. `zhigh.expand-mul-stick`). `NNPAAccelerator::conversionTargetONNXToKrnl()` installs a dynamic-legality callback on `ONNXFusedOp` that returns *illegal* for a `kind` starting with `zhigh.` and `std::nullopt` — defer to the pass's normal legality and pattern rules — for everything else. Deferring rather than declaring a non-`zhigh.` fused op legal is load-bearing: claiming legality stops the conversion driver from applying the other registered patterns (`ONNXFusedSplitOpGatherLowering`, `FusedOpInlineFallback`) to the op itself while it still independently descends into and converts the ops nested in its region, corrupting the fused op's body and terminator. Forcing the `zhigh.*`-kind ops through NNPA-specific lowering, `ZHighToZLow.cpp` registers dedicated patterns for each kind (`ZHighToZLowFusedExtLayoutTransformLowering`, `ZHighToZLowFusedExpandMulStickLowering`, `ZHighToZLowFusedConcatExpandStickLowering`, `ZHighToZLowFusedUnstickSplitHeadsLowering`, `ZHighToZLowFusedMulAddStickLowering`, all `FusedOpKindLowering<FusionT>` specializations) in `populateZHighToZLowConversionPattern`. This fusion is not restricted to any particular `DataLayout` — it matches on the surrounding IR shape, not on which layout the ztensor carries; see [concepts/nnpa-ztensor-layouts.md#layout-restricted-optimizations](nnpa-ztensor-layouts.md#layout-restricted-optimizations).

**Detection proves, verification re-checks.** `detectIfBeneficial()` always receives a non-null `DimAnalysis` (asserted in `FusedPatternForOpKind::matchAndRewrite`) and is the only place fusion legality is decided: every dynamic-dim equality the lowering relies on must be proven there with `sameDim`/`sameShape`. `verify()` runs at lowering time without `DimAnalysis`. It only confirms the body still has the structure and parameters detection recorded, and may accept `?` vs `?`. A hand-written `onnx.Fused` op therefore carries no such proof and must satisfy the dynamic-dim equalities itself. A kind may also override `absorbShapeConcatOfDims()` so that a small i64 shape `Concat` of constants/`onnx.Dim`s is cloned into the body rather than becoming an input; `zhigh.unstick-split-heads` does this because its `stick-3DS` Reshape shape is usually computed late in the block.[^17]

**Parallelism and loop collapse in the fused lowerings.** Under `--parallel`, the fused `expand-mul-stick`, `concat-expand-stick`, `unstick-split-heads`, and `mul-add-stick` lowerings each build a `KrnlParallelPlan`, subject to the `--parallelize-ops` op filter (empty by default, which admits every op). That plan may **collapse** several adjacent outer loop levels into one parallel region instead of parallelizing a single level. For `concat-expand-stick` in a decoder this matters because dim 0 is the dynamic batch (1 at decode), and a single-level region there would fork a thread team around one iteration. `NNPAAccelerator::rewritePatternONNXToKrnl()` passes `enableCollapse = enableParallel && !disableCollapse`, so collapse is **on by default whenever `--parallel` is on** and turned off by the general `--disable-collapse` flag (no NNPA-specific switch). See [stack/compiler.md](../../../../.agents/skills/onnx-mlir-internals/references/compiler.md) for `--disable-collapse` and the collapse cost-model overrides.[^18]

As of `aeb55f8` (added alongside the `concat-expand-stick` kind, to let it yield a second result): `FusedOpKindLowering<FusionT>::lowerVerified()` returns `FailureOr<SmallVector<Value>>` — one `Value` per `ONNXFusedOp` result, in `getOutputs()` order — rather than a single `Value`. `concat-expand-stick` returns one or two, `unstick-split-heads` returns `N` (one per Split result), and the other kinds return one. `FusionOpBasePattern`'s driver also gained a `computeInputsAndInsertionPoint()` check, run between `detectIfBeneficial()` and `fuse()` for every kind: it can fail even when a chain is otherwise matched (e.g. a chain-produced value's outside use feeds back into one of the chain's own external inputs, so no single safe insertion point exists), in which case the match is abandoned like any other failed pattern.

The kinds' matchers share a set of single-use helpers centralized in `src/Dialect/ONNX/ONNXOps/OpHelper.hpp`: `usedOnlyByOpType()` and its typed sibling `singleUserOfOpType()`, plus `uniqueUserOfOpType()` local to `ZHighFusionOpHelper.cpp`. `ExpandMulStickFusionHelper` additionally requires the `Mul`'s non-chain operand to be an `ONNXConstantOp` up front (via `matchValueAndOp`), since both scalar-extraction paths need one anyway.[^10]
